title: Queen María of Castile to Alfonso V, Valencia, 5 Aug 1435, ACA Cancillería reg. 3225 f. 59r (DECODE R10171)

plaintext.source: Register copy; no decipherment on the page, nothing in print. The king's register 2693 registers his ciphered letters in clear, but no clear copy of this letter was found.

transcription.notes: Three runs in the queen's letter (NOTES says four runs in one place, three in the table; cipher.txt has three). Some plain 8s carry a top-right stroke (8R), separated in cipher.txt.

system.summary: 42 graphic signs (digit-like, letter-like and dotted figures) in three runs inside clear Catalan; system not established.

diacritics.note: Dots flank three signs (square hook, bracketed b, circle with dot): probably word signs or nulls.

system.sibling_key: 1437 Montcada-Amat key (DECODE R10183): different alphabet. 1429 Castile-war key (Cortes & Pons, Saitabi 36, 1986): alphabet does not fit; its nomenclator seems to match the dotted word signs (hypothesis, four or five sign matches).
system.notes: Monoalphabetic annealing rejects every expected crib, pointing to homophones, nulls or syllabic signs; 42 signs cannot decide it.

prior_solution.where: Prior literature checked, nothing in print (NOTES); DECODE status non-decrypted.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the oldest-cipher candidate list (oldest/CANDIDATES.md A1). The image is public on DECODE. No target-specific intervention recorded in NOTES or git.
tools: annealer with Catalan quadgram model (solve.py, lm/catalan.txt)

solution.what: Full image of f. 59r fetched from DECODE R10171 without login.
Clear text of the three register items read; the three cipher runs transcribed sign by sign (cipher.txt, 42 signs).
Context: the truce of Majano expired 16 July 1435 and was extended; run 2 before 'es continuada daci a Tots Sants' = 'la treua [ab Castella]' as the leading crib.
Prior literature checked for a reading of the letter: nothing in print.
DECODE ACA keys: R10182 (1413) a jargon code; R10183, the 1437 Montcada-Amat alphabet, a different alphabet from the letter's.
Reg. 3226 (264 images) swept in full for sibling cipher: none.
Reg. 3224 (286 images) swept in full: no cipher.
Reg. 2693 (392 images) swept: no cipher signs or key, but 'Fuit expedita in cifra' entries including Alfonso to the queen, Gaeta 27 July 1435, 'In ciffra': a king-queen cipher in use that week.
Reg. 3113 (472 images) swept: no cipher. Cartas Reales Alfonso IV on PARES: no ciphered 1435 king-queen originals.

Printed 1429 Castile-war key (Cortes & Pons 1986) obtained and compared: alphabet does not carry over; nomenclator signs seem to match (regne d'Arago, Catalunya, rei de Castella, Navarra) as a hypothesis only.

Annealing, one sign = one letter, Catalan quadgram model, with and without the 1429 look-alike values and cribs (la treua, treua, tregua, castella, M z = es): every crib heavily penalised, output gibberish.

outcome.fraction_read_source: cipher.txt: 42 signs, none given a value (the nomenclator matches are a hypothesis)

gaps.detail: Needs reg. 3225's other 1435 folios (ACA, not digitised), the second key of B.A.H.M. ms. 677 ff. 160-161, or a queen-side key at the ARV; the 42 signs alone are too short.

outcome.notes: Attempted, closed from the evidence. No matched control was run for the 42-sign annealing; the negative rests on crib penalties, not on a control.
